title: Rename badge shows only the old basename — ambiguous for same-basename renames
description: PROBLEM: the rename badge shows only `← <old basename>`, with the full old path relegated to the tooltip. When two files in different directories were renamed from the same basename, their badges are visually identical — the user cannot tell the renames apart without hovering each one. NEEDED: disambiguate inline, e.g. show the shortest distinguishing suffix of the old path (only when two badges would otherwise collide, or always), or decide the tooltip is sufficient and close. (item 77)

title: renderFileHistoryView is a near-duplicate of the Revision View — consolidate?
description:
PROBLEM: two views implement the same per-revision UI independently. `renderFileHistoryView` (`webapp/views/file-history.ts:161`, route `#/project/

/file/`) renders per-revision rows with the *same five actions* as the Revision View's rev cards (Show content / Export this version / Copy patch / Export .patch / Jump to timeline step). Since item 84's bug-1 fix removed its `⤷` chip-row entry point, it is reachable only from the inspector's revision links and the snapshot pane's "View in File History" button — yet every future change to the five actions must be made in both places. NEEDED: consolidate — either retire `renderFileHistoryView` and repoint its two remaining entry points at the Revision View, or extract the shared revision-row rendering into one helper both views call. (item 84)

title: `⤷` snapshot-jump button renders for any matched changeId, not only snapshot-backed revisions
description: PROBLEM: the `⤷` snapshot-jump button is supposed to signal "this revision HAS a File History Snapshot", but its render condition doesn't check that. It renders whenever `computeSnapshotJumpRoute` returns a route, and that returns `undefined` only when the changeId is absent, resolves to no history, or resolves to a blob name with no anchored revision — i.e. the button appears for essentially any changeId that matches a revision, snapshot-backed or not. The indicator over-fires and misleads. NEEDED: tighten the render condition so `⤷` appears only for revisions actually backed by a snapshot, or redefine/document the button's meaning as "jumpable" rather than "snapshot-backed". (item 84)

title: Doubled rtk-rewrite tool-call rows (s39): signal, or collapse into the original row?
description: PROBLEM: when the rtk-rewrite hook rewrites a tool call, the timeline renders two rows for one logical action — the original and the rewrite. In s39 the hook rewrote both `ls` and `git add`, so the timeline shows `* git add … *` AND `* rtk git add … *`. This follows the locked "all tool calls, including hook rewrites" rule, but the doubled rows may read as noise rather than signal. NEEDED: decide whether doubled hook-rewrite rows stay as-is (two rows = signal) or a rewrite collapses into its original row (one row, two line labels); if collapsing, implement it in the timeline tool-call row rendering. (timeline tool-call rows)

title: Failed git commands still emit timeline rows and CommitMarkers — suppress or badge?
description: PROBLEM: git-op extraction never checks `is_error`, so a FAILED git command still contributes timeline rows. s6's compound `git add … && git commit` failed at runtime yet now contributes add+commit rows (its commit row has `resultHash: undefined` — error output carries no `[branch hash]` line); this mirrors how a failed plain `git commit` already gets a row today. Relatedly, `findGitCommitEvents` for s6 returns 2 commit events (failed compound + retry) where the repo has only 1 real commit — `resolveCommitByTimestamp` resolves both to the same commit (harmless for the evidence channel), but CommitMarkers (timeline pick hard-stops) now include the failed compound's instant; flag if a duplicate marker ever shows up as a visible artifact in the viewer. NEEDED: decide whether failed git commands should be suppressed or badged — a decision spanning ALL git ops, not just compound ones.
